full_caption: Two Rivers Homeowners Association, Inc., Appellant, v. Fitzwilliam Jarrowmere, Appellee
court: Ardenne Land and Property Court, Lindenmere Division
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Two Rivers Homeowners Association, Inc. and Fitzwilliam Jarrowmere own riparian tracts along the Sable Fork within Lindenmere County. The dispute concerns Fitzwilliam Jarrowmere's diversion of approximately 1,575 gallons per minute for irrigation of 2.7 acres.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The public trust doctrine reserves to the State title to the beds of navigable waters. Navigability for title purposes is determined by susceptibility to commercial navigation at the date of statehood.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The 31 days of well failure experienced by Two Rivers Homeowners Association, Inc. coincided with the operation of Fitzwilliam Jarrowmere's high-capacity irrigation well 50 feet from the shared aquifer boundary. Causation was established by drawdown modeling.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Severed mineral rights carry an implied easement to use so much of the surface as is reasonably necessary to extract the minerals, but that right is qualified by an obligation to accommodate existing surface uses where reasonable alternatives exist.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Reasonableness is a question of fact informed by the purpose of the use, its economic and social value, the extent of the harm, the practicality of avoiding the harm, and the protection of existing investments.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: The accommodation doctrine required Fitzwilliam Jarrowmere to consider directional drilling from an off-site pad before siting the wellpad within the irrigated circle. Failure even to evaluate the alternative defeats the claim of reasonable necessity.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: A prescriptive water right may be acquired by open, adverse diversion for the statutory period, but only as against a use that was actually interfered with during that period.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The injunction is modified to permit diversion not exceeding 300 gallons per minute between March and October, and is otherwise affirmed.

sections.heading: RIDER B — MINIMUM BYPASS FLOW AND MEASUREMENT
sections.text: A minimum bypass flow sufficient to satisfy downstream domestic and stock-watering needs shall be maintained at all times. Each diverting party shall install and maintain a totalizing meter at the point of diversion, shall record readings weekly, and shall furnish records to any other riparian owner within 5 days of written request. Domestic use has priority over irrigation, and irrigation over industrial use, in every period of shortage.

sections.heading: RIDER C — GROUNDWATER AND WELL INTERFERENCE
sections.text: No high-capacity well shall be completed within 50 feet of an existing domestic well without a drawdown analysis furnished to the affected owner. If operation of a high-capacity well causes an existing domestic well to fail or its yield to fall below five gallons per minute, the operator shall, at its expense, deepen or replace the affected well or provide an equivalent permanent supply. Withdrawal for export off the overlying tract is prohibited where it injures a neighboring overlying user.

sections.heading: RIDER E — BOUNDARY, ACCRETION AND PUBLIC TRUST
sections.text: Where the boundary is a watercourse, gradual accretion and reliction move the boundary with the water; a sudden and perceptible avulsive change does not, and the boundary remains at the former thread of the stream. Nothing in this instrument conveys any interest in the bed of a navigable water, title to which is held by the State in trust for the public.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Entire Agreement and Riders
sections.text: This instrument, together with the exhibits and riders attached and incorporated by reference, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations and agreements, whether oral or written. In the event of a conflict between a printed provision and a rider, the rider shall control, the rider being the specifically negotiated expression of the parties' intent.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Insurance
sections.text: The party in possession shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence, naming the other party as an additional insured, and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request and on each renewal. Each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds actually received.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Governing Law
sections.text: This instrument shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Ardenne, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Any action arising out of or relating to this instrument shall be brought exclusively in the courts sitting in Lindenmere County, Ardenne, and each party consents to the personal jurisdiction of those courts.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Inspection and Right of Entry
sections.text: Upon not less than twenty-four (24) hours' prior notice, and at reasonable times, a party may enter upon the subject premises to inspect, to make permitted repairs, or to show the premises to a prospective purchaser or lender. Entry without notice is permitted only in an emergency threatening life or substantial property damage, and the entering party shall give notice of the entry as soon as practicable thereafter.
